\chapter{Boolean Analysis — Projection Bounds}
%%% generated by the blueprint pipeline from TCSlib.BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.Randomization.ProjectionBounds
\section{Overview}
Walsh coefficients of randomization identify product components with sign-cube Fourier coefficients. Spectral identities and self-adjoint norm duality support the product low degree projection bounds.

\section{Declarations}

\begin{theorem}[Randomization Fourier coefficients]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.randomization_fourier_coefficient}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.Point, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.component, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.randomization, BooleanAnalysis.fourierCoeff, DecisionTree.fourierCoeff_sum_chiS}
\difficulty{1}
Let $P$ be a product of $n$ finite probability spaces with strictly positive atom masses and outcome space $\Omega=\prod_i\Omega_i$, $f:\Omega\to\mathbb R$, $x\in\Omega$, and $S\subseteq[n]$. The Walsh coefficient at $S$ of $r\mapsto R_rf(x)=\sum_T\chi_T(r)f_T(x)$ is $f_S(x)$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Degree of cube projection]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.RandomizationProjectionAux.cube_lowDegree_has_degree}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.BooleanFunc, BooleanAnalysis.has_degree_at_most, KKL.fourierCoeff_lowDegreePart, KKL.lowDegreePart}
\difficulty{3}
Let $f:\{0,1\}^n\to\mathbb R$ be a function on the uniform Boolean cube and $k\in\mathbb N$. The Fourier projection $f^{\le k}$ has Fourier degree at most $k$.
\end{theorem}

\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.RandomizationProjectionAux.cube_lowDegree_projection_noise_ge_two}

\begin{theorem}[Lifting pointwise randomization bounds]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.RandomizationProjectionAux.randomizationNorm_le_of_pointwise_cube_bound}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.Point, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.expect, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.expect_const_mul, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.cubeLpNorm, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.cubeLpNorm_rpow, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.expect_rpow_abs_nonneg, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.randomization, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.randomizationNorm, BooleanAnalysis.expect}
\difficulty{4}
Let $P$ be a product of $n$ finite probability spaces with strictly positive atom masses and outcome space $\Omega=\prod_i\Omega_i$, $f,g:\Omega\to\mathbb R$, $q>0$, and $A\ge0$. If $\|r\mapsto R_rf(x)\|_q\le A\|r\mapsto R_rg(x)\|_q$ on the uniform sign cube for every $x$, then $\|Rf\|_q\le A\|Rg\|_q$, where $\|Rh\|_q=(\mathbb E_{x\sim P}\mathbb E_r|R_rh(x)|^q)^{1/q}$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Components of low degree projection]

\begin{theorem}[Randomization commutes with noise]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.RandomizationProjectionAux.randomization_cube_noise}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.Point, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.noise, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.RandomizationAux.component_noise, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.randomization, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.randomization_fourier_coefficient, BooleanAnalysis.noiseOp}
\difficulty{3}
Let $P$ be a product of $n$ finite probability spaces with strictly positive atom masses and outcome space $\Omega=\prod_i\Omega_i$, $\rho\in\mathbb R$, $f:\Omega\to\mathbb R$, and $x\in\Omega$. Then $r\mapsto R_r(T_\rho f)(x)$ equals $T_\rho(r\mapsto R_rf(x))$, with the noise on the right acting on the uniform Boolean sign cube.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Randomization commutes with projection]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.RandomizationProjectionAux.randomization_cube_lowDegree}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.Point, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.lowDegree, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.RandomizationProjectionAux.component_lowDegree, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.randomization, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.randomization_fourier_coefficient, KKL.lowDegreePart}
\difficulty{3}
Let $P$ be a product of $n$ finite probability spaces with strictly positive atom masses and outcome space $\Omega=\prod_i\Omega_i$, $k\in\mathbb N$, $f:\Omega\to\mathbb R$, and $x\in\Omega$. Then $r\mapsto R_r(f^{\le k})(x)$ is the Fourier projection to levels at most $k$ of the function $r\mapsto R_rf(x)$ on the uniform Boolean sign cube.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Scaled self-adjoint norm duality]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.RandomizationProjectionAux.product_selfAdjoint_bound}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteNorms.selfAdjoint_contraction, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.Point, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.expect, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.mass, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.norm, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.RandomizationProjectionAux.product_norm_const_mul}
\difficulty{5}
Let $P$ be a product of $n$ finite probability spaces with strictly positive atom masses and outcome space $\Omega=\prod_i\Omega_i$, $q>1$, $A>0$, and an operator $T$ on real functions on $\Omega$. If $\mathbb E_P[(Tf)g]=\mathbb E_P[fTg]$ for every $f,g$ and $\|Tg\|_{q/(q-1),P}\le A\|g\|_{q/(q-1),P}$ for every $g$, then $\|Tf\|_{q,P}\le A\|f\|_{q,P}$ for every $f$.
\end{theorem}
